Ricardo @pine21b deviates somewhat from the norm in his analysis of medieval beastiaries in that he seeks to analyze their contents for discussions of evil in the medieval mind. Notable among these aims is his discussion of harms of deception and those of fear. Looking at harms grounded in a kind of deception, what is important here is that the three beasts associated with deception are also associated with pleasure. The relationship here is obvious. It is a relationship from a promise of pleasure to the end of the flourishing of the victim. The manticore imitates while the siren suduces.
